stories.title: ESRT’s 1359 Broadway Selling to Thor for $218M
stories.excerpt: Only a month after Commercial Observer learned it was going on the market, Empire State Realty Trust (ESRT) has found a buyer for 1359 Broadway in Thor Equities, which agreed to pay $218 million for the 22-story office building, according to sources. This is not much lower than the $225 million the 486,000-square-foot property was being shopped around for earlier this summer. Neither ESRT nor Thor responded to CO’s requests for comment. ESRT was represented by Newmark’s Adam Spies, Josh King, Adam Doneger, Avery Silverstein, Marcella Fasulo and Doug Harmon, who also did not respond to requests for comment by press time. CO was not able to learn who represented Thor. The property, just two blocks north of Herald Square, was 95 percent occupied as of last month, having inked recent leases with Infinium Wall Systems, SLCE Architects and nonprofit Braven, and has a Wolfgang’s Steakhouse and Wokuni in the retail portion. The purchase, expected to close in the next month or two and not official yet, is not Thor’s first dip into the Midtown office market this year. In March, CO reported that Joe Sitt’s company had purchased Michael Haddad’s 58,000-square-foot office and retail building, 1165 Broadway, for $56 million. Max Gross can be reached at mgross@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Empire State Realty Trust sells 1359 Broadway (486K SF office) to Thor Equities for $218M
Manhattan office building 95% leased; recent tenants include Infinium, SLCE Architects, nonprofit Braven
Sale price near asking ($225M); closing expected within 1–2 months
stories.summary: ESRT sold the 22-story office tower at 1359 Broadway in Midtown Manhattan to Thor Equities for $218 million, just $7 million below the initial ask. The 486,000-square-foot property was 95% occupied at sale, with recent leases from office and nonprofit tenants offsetting broader Manhattan office headwinds. The quick deal—marketed and sold within a month—suggests institutional investors remain willing to pay near-ask for high-occupancy, well-located office assets in Manhattan's core.
stories.impact: This signals that Manhattan office assets with strong occupancy and prime Herald Square adjacency retain value despite structural headwinds, but the buyer is a developer/operator (Thor), not a long-term hold fund. For multifamily: continued office-to-residential conversion optionality in Midtown if office fundamentals weaken further; monitor whether Thor intends value-add or conversion strategy.

stories.title: Finmarc Buys NoVA Office Complex for $78M
stories.excerpt: Finmarc Management has acquired a pair of office towers in Tysons, Va., for $77.5 million as the company begins another wave of acquisitions while doubling down on office space in Northern Virginia. The Bethesda, Md.-based investment firm acquired Highline at Greensboro from CIM Group. The two 10-story Class A buildings at 8401 and 8405 Greensboro Drive total roughly 460,000 square feet and were 70 percent leased at the time of the sale. “We remain buyers of office buildings and other assets in the greater DMV market, especially Northern Virginia because of our continued confidence in the regional market fundamentals,” Finmarc Principal Neil Markus said in a statement. Highline at Greensboro is near The Boro mixed-use complex and the Greensboro Metro station. The property features a fitness center, a golf simulator and a day care. Over the past two years, new tenants Mortgage One Solutions signed for 23,108 square feet and Tegna took 23,016 square feet. Cushman & Wakefield’s Paul Collins and Kevin Sidney represented CIM. Metropolis Capital Advisors’ Cliff Mendelson assisted Finmarc with the debt placement. Cushman & Wakefield’s Josh Masi and Paige Barger handle leasing at the Highline at Greensboro. Finmarc has been betting on discounted Northern Virginia offices. The company paid $51 million late last year for the nearly 620,000-square-foot Dulles Corner portfolio after acquiring the roughly 500,000-square-foot Trinity Centre for nearly $40 million the previous summer. The company funded the Highline acquisition partly with proceeds from three dispositions completed over the past six weeks, including office/flex and retail assets in Virginia and North Carolina. Finmarc also said it has more dry powder coming from expected sales over the next two to three months, and plans to reinvest the proceeds into another $250 million to $300 million of acquisitions. The firm currently owns and manages nearly 7.5 million square feet across the Mid-Atlantic. Gregory Corn
bullets: Finmarc buys Highline at Greensboro (460K SF, 2 Class A towers) in Tysons, VA for $77.5M
Property 70% leased; recent tenants Mortgage One (23K SF), Tegna (23K SF) signed within 2 years
Near Metro station, mixed-use corridor; Finmarc bullish on NoVA office fundamentals
stories.summary: Finmarc Management acquired Highline at Greensboro, a 460,000-square-foot, two-tower Class A office complex in Tysons Corner, from CIM Group for $77.5 million. The property was 70% leased at acquisition, with recent tenant wins from Mortgage One Solutions and Tegna signaling sustained demand. Finmarc's principal stated confidence in 'greater DMV market fundamentals,' particularly Northern Virginia, and flagged continued buyer appetite for office.
stories.impact: Finmarc's conviction in NoVA office—acquiring at 70% occupancy in a downtrodden asset class—reflects employer stability and job resilience in the Tysons/DMV corridor, likely driven by federal employment and defense contractors. For multifamily: sustained office leasing in NoVA supports worker population stability and suggests the metro remains a strong multifamily demand pocket; monitor whether office recovery there translates to faster apartment absorption and rent growth in adjacent submarkets.

stories.title: L3 Capital Secures 24K SF for Bylt Basics, Zara Flagships in Williamsburg
stories.excerpt: L3 Capital’s 108 North Sixth Street and 184-192 Bedford Avenue are welcoming two retail flagships to Williamsburg, Brooklyn. Men’s apparel brand Bylt Basics has selected 108 North Sixth Street, between Berry Street and Wythe Avenue, to host its first permanent New York City storefront, Commercial Observer has learned, in a bold signal of the retail corridor’s growing retail dominance. Fast fashion retailer Zara also plans to set up shop at L3’s nearby development down the block, 184-192 Bedford Avenue, according to a source familiar with the deals. Bylt signed on for 2,085 square feet at 108 North Sixth Street, and Zara’s new digs at 184-192 Bedford Avenue will span 22,060 square feet across three floors, according to the source. Zara will join current tenant Intuit TurboTax at the Bedford Avenue development. The Real Deal first reported the Zara lease. Spokespeople for Bylt and Zara did not immediately respond to requests for comment. L3 Capital was represented in both deals by a Newmark team of Ariel Schuster, Tyler King and Michael Paster, while MCD Retail’s Mitchell Dearman negotiated on behalf of Zara and Bylt. Spokespeople for L3 Capital, Newmark and MCD Retail did not respond to requests for comment. The asking rent for Bylt’s long-term lease was not disclosed, but retail rents inside nearby 184 Bedford Avenue vary from roughly $550 per square foot on the ground floor to $150 per square foot on the second floor. L3 Capital, a Chicago-based private equity firm, completed the redevelopment of 184-192 Bedford Avenue last year. The vacant, adjacent buildings that previously occupied the lots were demolished in 2022. L3 followed a similar playbook at 108-112 North Sixth Street, where it redeveloped three separate lots into a two-story commercial building in 2024. bullets: Bylt Basics opens first NYC flagship (2,085 SF) at 108 North Sixth Street, Williamsburg
Zara leases 22,060 SF across 3 floors at nearby 184–192 Bedford Avenue, Williamsburg
L3 Capital retail development in high-demand retail corridor; both leases from national tenants
stories.summary: L3 Capital signed two major retail tenants to Williamsburg, Brooklyn properties: Bylt Basics (men's apparel, 2,085 SF flagship at 108 North Sixth) and Zara (22,060 SF across three floors at 184–192 Bedford). Both represent national flagship or full-assortment retail, signaling strong confidence in Williamsburg's retail corridor dominance and foot traffic.
stories.impact: Retail flagship momentum in Williamsburg (retail rents, ground-floor economics, foot traffic) bolsters the submarket's mixed-use profile and attracts higher-income residents. For multifamily: retailers' capital commitment to Williamsburg retail validates demand for lifestyle-oriented urban renting; luxury and mid-market apartment developments in the corridor benefit from retail, dining, and entertainment amenities that support leasing velocity and pricing power.

stories.title: Nicola Offloads 143K-SF Chandler Business Park
stories.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield’s National Industrial Advisory Group arranged the sale of South Valley Business Park. The industrial assets total 143,813 square feet across two Class A buildings located at 1710 and 1720 East Germann Road in Chandler, Arizona. The buildings were originally developed in 2022 as a joint venture between Hopewell Development and Nicola Wealth Real Estate (NWRE), and were subsequently acquired by Nicola Wealth as an investment property later that same year. Cushman & Wakefield’s Will Strong, Jack Stamets, Molly Miller, Michael Matchett and Madeline Warren facilitated the transaction, representing both the seller and the undisclosed buyer.South Valley Business Park is fully leased to five tenants and benefits from modern industrial specifications designed to accommodate a wide range of manufacturing, distribution, and logistics users. EMD Electronics is a long-term tenant at the location. The property’s direct frontage along East Germann Road and immediate access to Loop 202 provide convenient connectivity to the greater Phoenix freeway network. The post Nicola Offloads 143K-SF Chandler Business Park appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Nicola Wealth offloads South Valley Business Park (143.8K SF, 2 Class A buildings) in Chandler, AZ
Built 2022; originally JV with Hopewell Development; fully leased to 5 tenants, including EMD Electronics
Strategic location on East Germann Road with Loop 202 freeway access; buyer undisclosed
stories.summary: Nicola Wealth Real Estate sold South Valley Business Park, a fully leased 143,813-square-foot industrial complex in Chandler, Arizona, to an undisclosed buyer. The two Class A buildings, built in 2022 as a joint venture and held since 2022, featured modern manufacturing and logistics specifications and remained 100% leased. Cushman & Wakefield represented both parties.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily. Industrial property turnover in Chandler reflects investor appetite for fully leased, modern logistics real estate in metro Phoenix's supply-chain-critical submarket; no signal regarding apartment demand or supply.

stories.title: Miami Design District Owners Land $125M to Build Mixed-Use Building
stories.excerpt: A joint venture led by the owners of the Miami Design District has secured $125 million in debt to add a mixed-use building designed by world-renowned Snøhetta within the luxury, open-air mall, property records show. French bank Crédit Agricole, representing a group of lenders, supplied the construction loan for the 120,000-square-foot Sweetbird North development, which will be covered in a stainless-steel veil housing 22,500 square feet of ground-floor retail and office space on the top floors. Located at 95 Northeast 40th Street, the eight-story project will sit across from the Alo and Alice and Olivia boutiques and abut the Museum Garage. The 0.3-acre site has long remained vacant, housing retail pop-ups and food carts. New York-based private equity firm Raycliff Capital is a sponsor of Sweetbird North alongside the original backers of the 18-block mall, Miami Design District Associates: Miami-based developer Craig Robins, LVMH-backed L Catterton Real Estate and Bernard Arnault’s family office. The financing comes as the Design District, home to Chanel and Hermes stores, is set to further expand. The same set of sponsors is developing a 25-story condo tower and a 12-story hotel, branded by luxury hotel Fouquet’s and designed by Pritzker Prize winner David Chipperfield, which has yet to break ground. Facing I-95, another 20-story, 107-unit tower remains under construction after Miami Design District Associates and other partners secured a $125 million construction loan last year. Close by, a Kengo Kuma-designed development with a San Ambroeus restaurant broke ground in June after landing $85 million in debt. A representative for Robins’s Dacra did not immediately respond to a request comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Miami Design District JV secures $125M construction loan from Crédit Agricole for Sweetbird North
120K SF mixed-use; 22.5K SF retail/office; 8-story project by Snøhetta on long-vacant site
Backers include Craig Robins, LVMH-backed L Catterton Real Estate, Raycliff Capital PE sponsor
stories.summary: A joint venture led by Miami Design District owners, with PE sponsor Raycliff Capital, closed $125 million in construction financing from Crédit Agricole for Sweetbird North, an eight-story, 120,000-square-foot mixed-use project. The Snøhetta-designed building will house 22,500 SF of ground-floor retail and office on a long-vacant 0.3-acre infill site within the luxury mall, with residential likely on upper floors (not explicitly stated).
stories.impact: Capital availability for luxury mixed-use development in Miami's Design District remains strong despite broader CRE headwinds; continued retail and residential growth in this submarket signals sustained high-income demand and tourism-driven leasing in Miami. For multifamily: apartment component (if any) in Sweetbird North will be luxury-positioned, competing with other high-end rental in the Design District; validate market absorption and pricing in this ultra-premium segment.

stories.title: Burlington Takes 44K SF at Bay Ridge Retail Center Development
stories.excerpt: Off-price retailer Burlington has inked a 44,070-square-foot retail lease at Century Marketplace, a new retail development coming to 458 86th Street in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, developer MCB Real Estate announced Tuesday. The site between Fourth and Fifth avenues is undergoing a $130 million mixed-use redevelopment to turn the former 14-lot Century 21 department store assemblage into a 95,000-square-foot retail center. MCB, which began the redevelopment last year, also signed a grocery store to 16,042 square feet of retail space at the property, but would not provide further details. The two leases bring the assemblage to 65 percent leased. The center is expected to open in 2028. “Century Marketplace is a huge win for Bay Ridge, breathing new life into a long-vacant site and boosting the foot traffic that keeps local small businesses thriving,” Kayla Santosuosso, who represents the area on the City Council, said in a statement. “By creating local jobs, supporting working families and energizing our streets, this project builds on our promise to make our neighborhood a safer, more affordable and lively place to live.” MCB and urban retail investment firm Osiris Ventures acquired the old Century 21 site in July 2025 for $47.5 million. The length of the Burlington lease and the asking rent were not disclosed. The average asking rent for retail space along 86th Street in Bay Ridge was $85 per square foot last year, according to the most recent Brooklyn retail report from the Real Estate Board of New York. MCB did not disclose the names of the brokers who represented the landlord and the tenant. “Century Marketplace demonstrates MCB Real Estate’s ability to execute complex structuring while delivering high-quality, attractive retail to dense markets,” Drew Gorman, a principal at MCB, said in a statement. “By bringing together a nationally recognized specialty grocery anchor, and top national retailers like Burlington, we are reigniting a well-known co
bullets: Burlington signs 44,070 SF lease at Century Marketplace (new retail, Bay Ridge, Brooklyn)
Unnamed grocer takes 16,042 SF; development now 65% leased; $130M mixed-use redevelopment
Opening 2028 on former 14-lot Century 21 assemblage; 95K SF total retail component
stories.summary: Off-price retailer Burlington committed to a 44,070-square-foot lease at Century Marketplace, a new $130 million retail-focused mixed-use development in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, on the footprint of the former Century 21 department store. An undisclosed grocery tenant also signed for 16,042 SF. The 95,000-square-foot retail center is now 65% leased and is expected to open in 2028.
stories.impact: Retail anchors (Burlington, grocer) signal developer and retailer confidence in Bay Ridge's demographic trajectory and foot-traffic potential post-redevelopment. For multifamily: retail-anchored mixed-use redevelopment in an underutilized outer-borough submarket typically includes residential; monitor the residential component pipeline, pricing, and absorption in Bay Ridge as this project reaches opening—could signal demand recovery in this historically affordable Brooklyn submarket and raise rents in nearby apartments.

stories.title: Creation, Crow Holdings Building 700K-SF Avondale Warehouse Facility
stories.excerpt: Creation in partnership with a real estate fund advised by Crow Holdings Capital, has begun construction on Avondale Tech Center, a three-building Class-A industrial campus spanning 38 acres and totaling approximately 700,000 square feet. The three buildings range from 212,184 to 254,264 square feet and feature 36-foot clear heights. The development will include tenant-focused outdoor amenities not typically found in industrial developments, such as dedicated gathering areas for each building, a walking path encircling the campus and shared pickleball courts. The campus is designed to serve advanced manufacturing, research and development and assembly operations, with target industries including pharmaceutical development, aerospace, semiconductor manufacturing and defense contracting. LGE Design Build is both the architect and general contractor for the project. Leading leasing efforts are Riley Gilbert along with John Lydon and Kelly Royle of JLL. Completion is targeted for Q3 2027. The post Creation, Crow Holdings Building 700K-SF Avondale Warehouse Facility appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Creation and Crow Holdings Capital begin construction on Avondale Tech Center (700K SF, 3 buildings)
38-acre Class A industrial campus; 36-foot clear heights; targets pharma, aerospace, defense, semiconductors
Completion Q3 2027; Riley Gilbert (JLL) leads leasing; LGE Design Build architect and contractor
stories.summary: Creation, in partnership with Crow Holdings Capital, started construction on Avondale Tech Center, a 700,000-square-foot, three-building Class A industrial campus on 38 acres near Phoenix. Designed for advanced manufacturing, R&D, pharmaceuticals, aerospace, and semiconductors, the project features 36-foot clear heights, tenant amenities, and is slated for completion in Q3 2027. JLL is leading leasing.
stories.impact: Large-footprint, mission-critical industrial development in Phoenix reflects strong demand from advanced manufacturing and aerospace sectors; signals supply-chain investment and job creation in the metro. For multifamily: construction employment and tenant occupancy at Avondale will drive worker population, particularly skilled manufacturing and R&D labor, supporting apartment demand in Phoenix submarkets within commuting distance; validate absorption and rents in nearby residential as leasing progresses.

stories.title: CBRE: U.S. and Canadian AI Jobs Grow 45% Year-Over-Year
stories.excerpt: The ranks of U.S. and Canadian tech talent skilled in artificial intelligence grew by 45% in the past year, with AI-related roles now accounting for nearly a third of U.S. tech-talent job listings and boosting office-leasing activity in top tech hubs, CBRE reported. The firm’s 13th annual Scoring Tech Talent report highlights the clustering of AI jobs: 37% of AI jobs in the U.S. are found in the San Francisco Bay Area, New York City, Seattle and Washington, DC, while in Canada, the concentration is even greater as Toronto, Montreal and Vancouver claim 60% of AI jobs. CBRE expects the AI industry’s momentum to benefit office markets in key hubs. That’s especially true in San Francisco, where AI companies have accounted for 30% of leasing activity, roughly 10 million square feet, since 2023. “There’s no denying that AI is reshaping the tech industry and job growth in general,” said Colin Yasukochi, executive director of CBRE’s Tech Insights Center in San Francisco. “Growth of AI jobs in the U.S. far outpaced the broader tech-talent category, which expanded by 1.8% last year even as the tech industry cut some non-AI jobs. Markets adding AI jobs are further cementing their status as tech talent capitals.” The post CBRE: U.S. and Canadian AI Jobs Grow 45% Year-Over-Year appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: CBRE: U.S./Canadian AI jobs grew 45% year-over-year; AI now 1/3 of U.S. tech job listings
37% of U.S. AI jobs concentrated in SF Bay, NYC, Seattle, DC; San Francisco AI leasing ~10M SF since 2023
AI companies drove 30% of SF office leasing; CBRE expects AI to boost office in tech hubs
stories.summary: CBRE's 13th annual Tech Talent report found AI-related roles grew 45% in the past year and now represent nearly one-third of U.S. tech job listings. Geographically concentrated: 37% of U.S. AI jobs are in San Francisco, New York, Seattle, and Washington, DC. In San Francisco alone, AI companies accounted for 30% of office leasing activity (roughly 10 million SF) since 2023, signaling a major driver of office demand in top tech hubs.
stories.impact: AI job concentration and office leasing momentum in San Francisco, NYC, Seattle, and DC creates strong macro tailwinds for multifamily demand in and around these tech hubs—AI talent draw and supporting service-sector jobs increase population inflows. For TCR: prioritize acquisition and development in SF Bay, NYC, Seattle, and DC submarkets with proximity to AI company clusters (South Bay/Peninsula for SF, Manhattan tech corridor for NYC, Bellevue/Redmond for Seattle, Clarendon/Crystal City for DC); AI-driven job growth de-risks apartment demand and rent growth in these metros over the next 3–5 years.

stories.title: PCCP, RPM Pick Up 358-Unit Arlington Multifamily Community
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between PCCP and RPM Living Investments has acquired Truman at Arlington Commons, a four-story multifamily community located at 505 E Lamar Boulevard in Arlington, TX. The property was developed and owned by The Nehemiah Company. Built in 2021, the property features 358 units with an average size of 807 square feet (sf), across floorplans ranging from 576 to 1,594 sf. The units feature 10-foot ceilings, with select units offering 14-foot ceiling heights. 4,900 square feet of ground-floor retail is occupied by Nehemiah Coffee Company. Truman at Arlington Commons is located in North Arlington, a centrally positioned pocket between Dallas and Fort Worth with direct access to Interstate 30. The location provides connectivity to Arlington’s primary employment and entertainment districts, including AT&T Stadium, Globe Life Field, and Texas Live!, which together attract more than 50 million visitors annually. PCCP has approximately $29.3 billion in assets under management on behalf of institutional investors . The post PCCP, RPM Pick Up 358-Unit Arlington Multifamily Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: PCCP and RPM Living acquire Truman at Arlington Commons (358 units) in Arlington, TX for undisclosed price
Built 2021; 807 SF avg units; 4.9K SF retail (Nehemiah Coffee); North Arlington location near AT&T Stadium
Centrally positioned between Dallas and Fort Worth; near 50M+ annual visitors from sports/entertainment venues
stories.summary: A PCCP–RPM Living joint venture acquired Truman at Arlington Commons, a 358-unit, four-story apartment community completed in 2021 in North Arlington, Texas. Units average 807 square feet with 10-foot ceilings (some 14-foot); ground-floor retail is occupied by Nehemiah Coffee. The location offers direct Interstate 30 access and proximity to major employment and entertainment anchors (AT&T Stadium, Globe Life Field, Texas Live!), which collectively draw over 50 million annual visitors.
stories.impact: Arlington multifamily acquisition by institutional buyers (PCCP, RPM) reflects confidence in North Texas apartment demand, anchored by stable sports/entertainment employment and visitor-driven service jobs. For multifamily: Arlington's geographic midpoint between Dallas and Fort Worth, plus major entertainment venues, positions the submarket as a strong demand pocket for workforce and tourist-adjacent apartment supply; validate market rent and occupancy trends in this DFW pocket as part of broader Texas portfolio strategy.

stories.title: Kidder Mathews Entering Dallas Market
stories.excerpt: Kidder Mathews is expanding into Dallas, Texas, with the addition of six brokers. Mart Martindale, Brandon Beeson, Wilson Stafford, John David Cobb, and Claire Schmeltekopf form an investment sales team, while Barrett Jones joins as a healthcare tenant advisory specialist. The move marks the firm’s first entry into Texas and expands its footprint to 20 offices across six states. The new office will serve the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex and be led by former Edge Capital Markets co-founders Mart Martindale, Brandon Beeson, and Wilson Stafford. Together with Cobb and Schmeltekopf, they have completed more than $3.5 billion in transactions and have valued more than $20 billion in assets. Their clients include KeyBank, EPR Properties Trust, Trigild, BH Properties, Argentic Investment Management, and CWCapital, to name a few. In addition, Barrett Jones joins Kidder Mathews in Dallas, specializing exclusively in healthcare tenant representation. Mart Martindale joins as Senior Vice President, Managing Director, and Shareholder. The post Kidder Mathews Entering Dallas Market appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Kidder Mathews enters Dallas market with 6 new brokers; first Texas office
Investment sales team (Martindale, Beeson, Stafford, Cobb, Schmeltekopf) with 3.5B transacted, 20B valued
Barrett Jones joins as healthcare tenant advisory specialist; expands firm to 20 offices, 6 states
stories.summary: Kidder Mathews expanded into Dallas with six new brokers, marking its first entry into Texas. The new office is led by investment sales specialists (former Edge Capital Markets co-founders Martindale, Beeson, Stafford) and includes healthcare tenant advisory. The team has completed over $3.5 billion in transactions and valued $20 billion in assets, serving major institutional clients. Kidder Mathews now operates 20 offices across six states.
stories.impact: Kidder Mathews' Dallas entry and institutional brokerage presence signals confidence in DFW market depth and capital deployment; however, this is a brokerage/services event with limited direct signal on apartment supply or demand fundamentals. For TCR: use Kidder Mathews' Dallas team as a resource for market intel on capital flow, investor sentiment, and institutional investment activity in DFW; healthcare specialist addition suggests ongoing healthcare real estate investment in the region.
